skill.name: firebase-security-rules-auditor
skill.description: Audits Firebase Firestore security rules for access control, data validation, update bypass, and privilege escalation weaknesses.
skill.summary: Review Firestore rules for secure authorization, validation, and ownership controls.
skill.author: firebase

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses escaped Markdown backticks around Firestore rule helper names hasOnly() and diff(). No shell command, script, or execution instruction is present.
Line 14 discusses update bypasses in Firestore documents as part of an application security checklist. It does not request host reconnaissance or system enumeration.
Line 19 asks the model to verify ownership checks in Firestore rules. The wording concerns authorization logic, not local system discovery.

content.value_statement: Firestore rules can accidentally allow data leaks, role escalation, or unsafe updates. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a focused review of access control and validation gaps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews create and update rule differences for update bypass risk.
Checks whether sensitive authority fields rely on user-supplied document data.
Evaluates ownership checks around hasOnly() and diff() field restrictions.
Identifies missing type checks, string limits, and array size limits.
Scores rule sets from critical to secure with remediation guidance.
Considers hardcoded admin email bootstrapping when email verification is required.
limitations: Focuses on Firestore security rules, not Firebase Storage rules unless provided.
Does not run Firebase emulators or prove exploits with live requests.
Requires current rules and app context for accurate business-logic review.
Cannot replace a full application penetration test or production monitoring.

use_cases.title: Pre-Release Rules Review
use_cases.description: Check new Firestore rules before deployment and identify authorization or validation gaps.

use_cases.title: Security Triage
use_cases.description: Prioritize rule weaknesses by severity and convert them into concrete remediation tasks.

use_cases.title: Product Logic Validation
use_cases.description: Verify that rules support collaboration, ownership, and admin workflows without unsafe shortcuts.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Rules Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small rule set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Firestore security rules. Summarize the main risks, assign a 1 to 5 score, and list practical fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Update Bypass Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for create and update differences.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these rules for update bypasses. Compare create and update validation for roles, ownership fields, sizes, and data types.

prompt_templates.title: Ownership and Role Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit whether these rules trust user-provided authority fields. Check ownerId, role, isAdmin, and collaborator access paths.

prompt_templates.title: Release Gate Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release-gate audit for these Firestore rules. Include severity, exploit scenario, affected workflow, and recommended rule changes.

output_examples.input: A rule lets authenticated users update profile display names with hasOnly() but has no ownership check.
output_examples.output: Major finding: field restrictions limit what changes, but not who can change another profile. Add an ownership check before allowing updates.

output_examples.input: A create rule validates field types, but the update rule allows any new data for the same document.
output_examples.output: Critical finding: the update path can bypass create validation. Reuse the same type, size, and allowed-field checks for updates.

output_examples.input: An admin rule checks a fixed email and also requires email_verified to be true.
output_examples.output: Minor or no issue: this limited bootstrap pattern can be acceptable when no rule lets users add new admins or bypass verification.

best_practices: Provide complete rules, collection purpose, and expected user roles before asking for review.
Ask for separate findings for data leaks, privilege escalation, validation bypass, and denial-of-service risk.
Use the recommendations to update rules, then run a second audit on the revised version.
anti_patterns: Do not audit isolated snippets without explaining the app workflow and user roles.
Do not treat hasOnly() or diff() as ownership checks by themselves.
Do not accept a high score when update rules skip validation used during create.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits Firestore security rules for authorization, ownership, validation, and business-logic weaknesses.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it test rules against a live Firebase project?
faq.answer: No. It provides reasoning-based review and recommendations, not live emulator or production testing.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the full Firestore rules file, user roles, collection purposes, and sensitive fields.

faq.question: How should I use the score?
faq.answer: Use the score as a triage signal, then fix every critical and major finding before release.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps find common rule weaknesses, but high-risk applications still need expert review and testing.
